title: Walsh character identity for a finite field generator
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $\ell>0$. Choose a monic irreducible polynomial of degree $\ell$ over $\mathbb F_2$ to represent the binary extension field, and use its coefficient representation to perform arithmetic in that field. For $\gamma\in\mathbb F_2^n$ and $r,s$ in the represented field, form the vector whose $i$th coordinate is the binary dot product of the coefficient vectors of $r^{i+1}$ and $s$. The Walsh character indexed by this vector, evaluated at $x$ as prescribed by the generator, equals the Walsh character indexed by the coefficient vector of $\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}\gamma_i r^{i+1}$, evaluated at the coefficient vector of $s$.
hypotheses_covered: A chosen monic modulus whose polynomial is irreducible
Field elements $r,s$ in the represented binary extension field
caveat: The statement equates characters on different coordinate spaces via coefficient encodings; the supplied definitions specify the arithmetic representation but not an informal convention for the Walsh character.
